tasks.short: Complete death certificates and assign cause.

steps.what: Read the death notes already written.
Accept the wording of the death certificates.
Complete death certificates from the accepted version.

tasks.design: The coroner assigns cause and manner from the examination notes, accepts that wording, and only then is the same wording stored on the case file. A tool does not assign either one. Where national rules require a signature, the coroner still signs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cause and manner are a judgement on a particular death, not a field that can be copied from a form.
tasks.enabler_now: The case file can hold the wording the coroner has already accepted, so it is not typed twice.
tasks.still_hard: Two plausible causes can fit one set of notes, and the wrong one changes the legal record.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner assigns cause and manner and accepts the certificate. The file stores that version.
tasks.altitude: The assignment of cause and manner stays with the coroner. The case file holds the certificates only after they have accepted the wording.

reach.task: Hold the certificate the coroner accepted
reach.learn: Cause and manner were assigned by the coroner

evidence.claim: A case file can store certificate wording the coroner has already accepted, without assigning cause or manner.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the examination notes exist and ends when the accepted wording is on the case file. The examination itself, and any handwritten signature the register still requires, stay outside it.
The fields are case id, cause, manner, and the coroner's acceptance. The coroner produces cause and manner from the notes. If a field is missing, they type it. Nothing is inferred.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the assignment. They disagree only about a second typing of wording the coroner has already accepted.
Upkeep is keeping the certificate field names aligned with the case file.
unknowns: Whether the register still requires a handwritten signature besides the case file.
Which cause and manner values the register will accept.
research_questions: Does the register still require a handwritten signature?
Which cause and manner values will the register accept?

already_counted.description: Assigning the cause stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the certificate field names aligned with the case file

approvals.approved_version: death certificates the coroner accepted after assigning cause and manner

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If a handwritten signature is still required, that signature stays and the low end is only the case-file copy of wording already accepted. Assigning cause and manner stays either way. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Perform medicolegal examinations of the body.
Conduct autopsies and locate signs of trauma.
Identify factors that indicate time of death.

tasks.design: The coroner performs the examination and the autopsy, locates trauma, and identifies the factors that indicate time of death. No camera reading and no tool names a finding.
tasks.previous_blocker: The finding is in the body, and it changes as the examination proceeds.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new takes the examination off the coroner.
tasks.still_hard: A missed injury changes the cause that is assigned later, in another task.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner sees the body and names what is there. A photograph is not the examination.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The examination, the autopsy, and the time-of-death factors stay with the coroner.

reach.task: Receive a body the coroner has examined
reach.learn: The examination was done by the coroner

evidence.claim: A medicolegal examination and an autopsy are physical work on a body, and the findings are the coroner's.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the body is presented and ends when the coroner has identified the factors they will rely on. Writing the certificate is a separate task.
No fields are generated. The coroner may write notes by hand. Those notes are not transcribed by a tool in this task.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. None of the time is counted as saved.
Upkeep is zero because no screen and no list are added.
unknowns: Which examinations this office expects the coroner to perform rather than a pathologist.
Which samples must be sent to a laboratory.
research_questions: Which examinations does the coroner perform rather than a pathologist?
Which samples must go to a laboratory?

incremental.description: No screen or list is added, so there is nothing to keep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case and the centre are the same. The examination and the autopsy do not shrink, so the saving is zero. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.short: Interview people present at the death scene.

steps.what: Interview persons present at the death scene.
Obtain information useful to the later inquiry.
Hear what they saw of the death.
Leave the manner of death unset in this interview.

tasks.design: The coroner interviews the people present and obtains what they saw. The manner of death is not set in the interview, and the conversation is not recorded as audio.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each answer changes the next question, and people at a scene are distressed.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new takes the interview off the coroner.
tasks.still_hard: A person may be a witness, a relative, or both, and they may not want to talk.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner decides what to ask and what to believe. A form does not.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. Interviewing people at the scene stays with the coroner, and the manner of death is not set there.

reach.task: Use an account the coroner heard in person
reach.learn: The interview was conducted by the coroner

evidence.claim: An interview at a death scene is a conversation the coroner conducts, and it is not a recording.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a person at the scene can be spoken to and ends when the coroner has heard them. Determining manner of death is a separate task. No audio is stored.
No fields are generated. The coroner may write a few words afterwards by hand. This task does not transcribe them.

Upkeep is zero because no recorder and no question list are added.
unknowns: Who may be interviewed before a relative has been told.
Whether a second person must be present for some interviews.
research_questions: Who may be interviewed before a relative has been told?
When must a second person be present?

tasks.short: Observe and record bodies and evidence.

steps.what: Observe related evidence at the scene.
Write notes on the positions and conditions.
Review the positions and conditions note.
Record the accepted note of the evidence.

tasks.design: The coroner observes positions, conditions, and related evidence, writes the note, and reviews it. The case file then stores that note. It does not describe the scene for them.
tasks.previous_blocker: The positions exist only at the scene, and they are disturbed as soon as people move.
tasks.enabler_now: A note the coroner has written and reviewed can be stored without a second handwriting.
tasks.still_hard: A body and the evidence around it have to be seen, not summarised from a photo.
tasks.human_edge: The coroner observes and writes. The file holds the note they reviewed.
tasks.altitude: Observing the scene stays with the coroner. The record is the note they reviewed after that observation.

reach.task: Read the scene note the coroner reviewed
reach.learn: The positions were observed by the coroner

evidence.claim: A scene note the coroner has written can be stored as they reviewed it, after they have observed the bodies.

Assigning cause or manner of death, certifying a death, and arranging care for a child are determinations the coroner makes. A tool does not make them. National rules decide who may certify a death. EU data-protection rules cover medical details and living relatives. The file stores only what the coroner recorded, and interviews are not stored as audio.

assumptions: The workflow starts at the scene and ends when the reviewed note is on the case file. Moving the body is a separate task.
The fields are case id, position, condition, and the evidence the coroner named. The coroner produces them by looking and writing. A blank is left blank.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the observation and the handwriting. Only the copy of a reviewed note is shorter.
Upkeep is keeping the scene-note headings stable.
unknowns: Whether photographs are already attached to the case before the note is written.
Who else is allowed to add a line to that note.
research_questions: Are photographs already on the case before the note is written?
Who else may add a line to the scene note?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the coroner already writes the note straight into the case file, the second copy disappears and the low end is the observation, the handwriting, and the review, which stay. Provisional, not a measured result.

role.altitude: The examination, the autopsy, and the interview at the scene stay with the coroner. Cause and manner are assigned by them before any certificate is stored. A scene note is filed only after they have observed the bodies and reviewed the note.
reach: A registrar holds certificate wording the coroner accepted
An investigator reads a scene note written after the coroner observed the bodies
skills_to_grow: Assigning cause and manner before the certificate is stored
Leaving manner of death unset during the scene interview
Reviewing a scene note only after the observation
role.ambitious_version: Every certificate states a cause and a manner the coroner assigned, and every scene note was reviewed after they saw the body.
